d: Linear collections of data elements where each points to the next.

p: Unlike arrays, Linked List nodes are scattered in memory. Each node holds data and a pointer to the next node. Reversing a linked list is the most common foundation for advanced list problems.

def reverseList(head):
  prev, curr = None, head
  while curr:
    nxt = curr.next
    curr.next = prev
    prev = curr
    curr = nxt
  return prev
Time: O(N) single pass. Space: O(1) pointers.

[Head] -> [Node A] -> [Node B] -> [Tail] -> null
  |          |           |
Data: 1    Data: 2     Data: 3
Next: A    Next: B     Next: null
